name: Rhein
description: Rhein (CAS 478-43-3 ), also known as Cassic acid and Rhubarb Yellow, is an anthraquinone compound derived from rhubarb root and related botanical sources. It functions as a natural colorant, antioxidant, and UV-stabilizing agent across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and industrial applications. In personal care formulations, it is incorporated as a natural yellow pigment and antioxidant active, particularly in products targeting skin tone evenness and photoprotection. The textile and leather industries use it as a natural dye capable of imparting yellow to orange hues. This compound is applied to protein-based and cellulosic fibers, often in combination with mordants to improve wash fastness. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a reference standard and active ingredient in preparations derived from traditional botanical extracts. It contributes to the documented bioactivity of rhubarb-based formulations in various medicinal contexts. In paper processing, it is evaluated as a surface-modifying agent that influences substrate wettability and coating adhesion for specialized industrial uses. The material is supplied as a yellow to orange crystalline powder for ease of handling. It is available in research-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 95% to 98%+ by HPLC analysis. Botanical extract standardized forms are also commercially available for buyers sourcing at scale for cosmetic or nutraceutical applications.
